Annual Report and Financial Statements for the year ended 31March 2025
Strategic Report
The directors present their Strategic Report and the audited financial statements of Chetwood Financial Limited and its subsidiaries
('Chetwood' or 'the Group') for the year ended 31 March 2025.
Chetwood Financial Limited is a digital UK retail bank. It is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial
Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority, under registration number 740551.
The principal activities of the Group are the provision of banking services. Chetwood owns Yobota Limited, a technology company, and
CHL Mortgages for Intermediaries Ltd ('CMI'), a specialist buy-to-let mortgage lending business. CMI became a wholly owned subsidiary

Review of the business
Chetwood has made significant progress in the financial year, with an improved financial performance, considerable growth in its net
lending book, and continued investment in its underlying infrastructure and product proposition, including in particular, the acquisition of
CMI and the launch of Moda Mortgages.
CMI was acquired on May 20, 2024, when Chetwood purchased 100% of the share capital of the business for total consideration of £8m.
The fair value of assets acquired, and liabilities assumed was £3.5m, resulting in goodwill of £4.5m. There was no contingent consideration.
CMI had operated a forward flow line with Chetwood since Q4 2023, whereby it originated and sold mortgage assets to Chetwood. The
acquisition enables Chetwood to further expand and grow its presence in the buy-to-let (BTL) lending space, with CMl's more specialist
approach to lending complementing the more automated approach taken by Chetwood's organic mortgage lending business, Moda
Mortgages ('Moda'), which launched in July 2024.
As well' as lending BTL mortgages on its own behalf, Chetwood continues to utilise its knowledge of UK consumer asset classes to
opportunistically acquire mortgage and consumer loans from external parties by way of forward flow arrangements and whole loan
portfolio purchases.
With the launch of Moda and the acquisition of CMI, Chetwood is building a significant presence in the UK specialist BTL mortgage space,
which, when combined with its forward flow acquisition business, saw it write more than £lbn of mortgage loans onto the balance sheet
in the financial year.
Chetwood also provides senior finance to seċuritisation companies and significantly developed its senior securitisation finance business
through the year, building on its structured finance expertise to invest directly into wholesale finance warehouse facilities as well as via
the public securitisation markets. At the year end, the Group had secured investment positions in two securitisation warehouse facilities,
with £17Om funded against a potential £20Om overall commitment, and a total senior securitisation exposure of £696m. The Group will
continue to further develop this business line over the next financial year.
In December, the Company purchased a £7Om portfolio of unsecured consumer loans for  total consideration of £41m from a related
party. The portfolio represented loan exposures that Chetwood had previously originated and sold under a forward flow arrangement.
In order to fund its balance sheet growth, Chetwood has invested heavily in its retail savings proposition, including the rebrand of its
deposit business to Chetwood Bank, and the launch of an organic Easy Access product, which had successfully raised £635m by the year
end. Chetwood's retail savings proposition continues to go from strength to strength, with the book growing by £956m over the year to
reach £3.8bn at the year end.
During the year, aligned to the Group's strategic pivot from in-house to third party sourced and outsourced technology and services, the
Group Board Audit Committee has continued to receive regular updates on management's ongoing activities for improving the Bank's IT
environment and the effective oversight of end-to-end business processes also at forward flow partners.
Management continued to identify opportunities for enhancing key controls, such as through the use of IT led solution, outsourcing.
automation technologies as well as monitoring controls.

At the year end 99.3% (2024: 96.6%) of the gross loan boók was secured mortgage assets or senior securitisation positions. As a result of
the further growth in secured lending, the overall provision coverage has reduced to O.4% of gross loans held at amortisęd cost (2024:
1.6%), versus a coverage ratio of 36.84% (2024: 45.3%) against unsecured assets held at amortised cost.
Whilst the proportion of unsecured assets on its balance sheet is significantly smaller, the Group nonetheless recognises that despite the
decrease in the overall provision coverage, the risks to the performance of the unsecured book have remained heightened. This is a key
driver of the £1.7m impairment loșs in the Consolidated Statement of Total Comprehensive Income (2024: £O.9m).
On the liabilities side, customer deposits increased to £3,812m (2024: £2,857m), with the bank benefiting in particular from its newly
launched Easy Access product. It has managed to maintain an attractive cost of funds throughout the period, despite banking funding
costs rising more generally across the market.
The Group's funding capability has also benefitted from the approval by the Bank of England of Chetwood's inaugural securitisation as

the year, supplementing the bank's retail savings proposition.
The growth in the balance sheet and significantly improved revenue performance was offset to some extent by the continued significant
investment in the Group's underlying banking infrastructure and lending capabilities. Nonetheless, the Group still saw a reduction in its
loss after tax for the year to £4.7m (2024: £8.9m).
The continued significant investment during the financial year has focused predominantly on three particular areas; firstly in the building
its organic mortgage lending business, Moda Mortgages, which launched in July 2024, had contributed £12.6mi to the gross loan book by
year end and is now providing the business with a route to generate significant volumes of high quality organic BTL mortgages, as well as
the subsequent ability to innovate into other ancillary secured asset classes in time.
Secondly, the business has focused on the development of a more substantial retail deposit offering, which will enable Chetwood to
organically originate deposit volumes across the Easy Access and short-term fixed savings markets. Finally, the business has invested in
transitioning from internally built software (in particular via its Yobota banking platform) to more generic third party software. This latter
change is seen as vital to ensuring that Chetwood is able to deliver a streamlined and efficient cost base, and with lower contingent risk
in the maintenance and development of the firm's tech estate.

nonetheless enabled the Group to progress significantly towards its goal of growing sustainably and reaching profitability in the coming

The Group is fortunate to have had the continuing support of its shareholders during this period, as well as the commitment of dedicated
employees.
Future developments
The principal investor has demonstrated their continued support of the Group's growth plans by injecting £27m of capital during the year
and a further £2Om between the balance sheet date and the date of signing. Further capital injections are anticipated in the coming year,
to support growth predictions.

to build lending and savings trading volumes and to launch further organic mortgage and savings products, including in particuilar, a notice
product offering.The Group remains acquisitive and is looking to both expand its investment classes and grow the senior securitisation
funding business, after successfully launching this in the financial year.
The Group recognises the risks to business performance associated with the current macroeconomic uncertainty, and that the impact
may be amplified for a business such as Chetwood, which needs further growth in its balance sheet and lending activities to reach and
sustain profitability.
Risk management
The Board recognises the importance of having a robust risk culture and supports the key factors that contribute to an open and
transparent environment, where knowledgeable and skilled individuals take intelligent risk decisions aligned to clear policies, in pursuit of
the Group's defined strategy.

The Group presents realised and unrealised gains and losses on loans and advances held at fair value in net income from financial
instruments held at fair value through profit and loss per Note 6. Within settlements / repayments is the write off of irrecoverable loans.
Loans and advances are valued using a discounted cash flow methodology, the significant unobservable inputs to the model are the
probability of default, loss given default, expected prepayment rates and the market discount rate. Significant increases in any of these
inputs in isolation would result in lower fair values. Expected prepayment rates are derived from historical prepayment trends,
probabilities of default and loss given default are derived from historical default and recovery information and adjusted for current
conditions.

37 Capital management
The Company is subject to supervision by the PRA as an authorised bank. -The amount of capital held is measured against the regulatory
framework defined by the Capital Requirements Regulation ('CRR'). The Board manages capital levels for both current and future activities,
models stress scenarios and documents its risk appetite as part of the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP). Chetwood
has previously been granted a solo-consolidation waiver by the PRA, allowing Chetwood to incorporate subsidiaries in the calculation of
its capital requirement under CRR Article 6(1). The regulatory capital requirements are therefore shown at a Group level only.
Current and forecast levels of capital resources are monitored and reviewed by the Board and management on a regular basis. The Group

38 Related parties
Parties are considered to be related if one party has the ability to control the other party, exercise significant influence over the other
party, or one other party controls both.
On 12 December 2024, Chetwood Financial Limited paid £41m (2024: £O.2m) to purchase gross loans and advances with a par value of
£70m (2024: £O.2m) from Cherub, a remote legal entity, related by common ultimate control. Chetwood originated these loans and
continued to service them until the purchase and Cherub paid £O.4m (2024: £1.1m) in servicing fees to the Group. As at the balance sheet
date, an amount of £nil (2024: £62k) was due to Chetwood in relation to servicing fees.
Chetwood Financial Limited has a forward flow arrangement with Enra Specialised Finance Limited, whereby the Group purchases to order
newly originated mortgage assets. Enra Specialist Finance Limited is a remote legal entity, related by common ultimate control. At the
balance sheet date £230.9m (2024: £173.4m) of secured loans and advances have been purchased on origination. An Enra Specialised
Finance Limited group company, West One Secured Loans Ltd remains the servicer of these assets, during the year Chetwood has been
invoiced £435k (2024: £266k) in servicing and origination fees. With £nil (2024: £40k) remaining due at the balance sheet date. The
balance due is unsecured and payable on 30 day invoice terms.
Chetwood Financial Limited leased a commercial premises from a company deemed a related party due to a common person of significant
influence. The payments made during the year totalled £40k (2024: £243k), with £nil (2024: £nil) due to be paid as at the balance sheet
date. The lease was exited during the year.

During the previous year, Chetwood undertook a fully retained securitisation of mortgage assets, with a carrying value of £1,120.8m. The
beneficial title of the assets was legally sold into a securitisation company, Chetwood Funding Limited 2024-1 ('CFL 2024-1'), however
Chetwood Financial Limited retains the risk and reward of the assets, therefore the assets remain on the Chetwood balance sheet both
on a company and consolidated basis. Chetwood accounts for the securitisation net, reducing the deemed loan balance by the principal
of the A and Z loan notes due.
Chetwood retains the risk and reward of the mortgages underlying the deemed loan and remits all collections on these mortgages to CFL
2024-1. At year end there was an additional £8,374k intercompany balance due to the Company from CFL 2024-1(2024: £3,985k due
from the Company to CFL 2024-1).
